basics.name: Nico Loesch
basics.headline: Machine Learning Engineer · Clinical NLP, LLMs & Medical Imaging

summary.content: Machine learning engineer with a PhD in Computer Science and a background in medical engineering. I build NLP and LLM systems for electronic health records on the OMOP Common Data Model, from ETL and ontology grounding to RAG and agentic AI, and maintain the open-source OMOP tooling behind them. PhD research in medical image segmentation using diffusion models and weak supervision.

items.description:
• Develop a scalable ETL pipeline for large-scale EHR analysis that maps clinical records to the OMOP Common Data Model, combining rule-based NLP and LLMs.

  • Built the pipeline's RAG concept-retrieval layer, grounding extracted clinical entities to standard OMOP vocabularies through a virtual knowledge graph and vector store.

  • Prepared the pipeline's backend for agentic AI, exposing the knowledge graph and vector store as tools for LLM agents via MCP and ACP.

  • Released the core components as open-source libraries (omop-alchemy, omop-graph, omop-emb; see Contributions), with full CI/CD in GitHub Actions.

• Fine-tuned and prompt-engineered LLMs to analyse social media text, enabling automated detection of cancer burden.

  • Applied transformer-based language models for semantic analysis, topic modelling and clustering of large-scale social media data.

• Developed software for navigated robotic surgery in an agile team using CI/CD practices.

  • Validated software implementations to ensure reliability and compliance with medical device standards.

• Developed a labelling GUI for medical image segmentation.

  • Developed real-time control algorithms for robotic arm manipulation, including gaze and head tracking with VR headsets.

• Weakly-supervised brain tumour segmentation of multi-modal MRI using diffusion models.

  • Multi-disciplinary research in collaboration with the Children’s Hospital at Westmead, Sydney.

  • Thesis: Towards Robust Clinical Segmentation of Paediatric Brain Tumours in Magnetic Resonance Imaging Using Weakly-supervised Deep Neural Networks, supervised by Prof. Paul Kennedy and Prof. Daniel Catchpoole.

  • Academic tutor for Fundamentals of Data Analytics and Databases (2022–2025).

• Erasmus exchange semester at Lund University, Sweden.

  • Thesis: Efficient Medical Image Segmentation with Graph Neural Networks, supervised by Marc Fischer and Prof. Bin Yang (Grade: 1.3/5.0).
• Thesis: Development of a Protocol to Quantify Spatially-resolved Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy in Neurology, supervised by Dr. Andreas Schmid (Grade: 1.6/5.0).

items.name: omop-graph
items.description: Maintainer. Built the virtual knowledge graph over the OMOP vocabulary, with embedding integration and a full resolver pipeline for concept retrieval, preparing it for agentic traversal.

items.name: omop-alchemy
items.description: Maintainer. Typed SQLAlchemy ORM for the OMOP Common Data Model; delivered performance improvements, schema-aware database handling and DuckDB integration.

items.name: omop-emb
items.description: Maintainer. Built from the ground up: vector-embedding and RAG store for OMOP concepts with sqlite-vec, pgvector and FAISS backends.

items.name: TorchIO
items.description: Contributor to the PyTorch library for 3D medical imaging. Fixed a memory leak in subject copying and a spatial-shape bug in RandomAnisotropy; added inverse support for RescaleIntensity and argument propagation to nested transforms.
